_notes: The prior's desk. E3 §3.2: the house's budget is held in common and controlled by the prior, its observance is his to set, and the offices of the house are in his gift (§3.10). Rules are a target the house's observance drifts toward, a point or so a week, and a house being moved rubs: the men who like where it was going lose a little regard for him, and cohesion dips while it moves. Purse spends are one-off draws on the house's budget with a cooldown in weeks. Tunables invented. Builds are multi-year projects from the house's budget, one at a time; the province may be asked for a grant of half; each adds a building, sometimes a work, and draws vocations. Vocations: a house draws men every year on its kind, its works, its observance and cohesion, its buildings, and its prior's name (systems/religious/growth.ts).

rules.label: The mitigated observance
rules.line: Vespers when enough men are home, the habit for Mass, the door open. The old men are relieved and the observant ones write to the provincial.

rules.label: As the province keeps it
rules.line: The Office in common most days, the habit in the house, the table together at noon. Nobody writes to anyone.

rules.label: The full observance
rules.line: The Hours sung, the habit worn, the silence kept after Compline. The house is proud of it in about a year and tired of it in two.

rules.label: The primitive observance
rules.line: Matins, the fast, the enclosure kept, recreation at the hour and not after. Some men flower under it and some ask for a transfer.

purse.label: The library
purse.blurb: A year's acquisitions, the binding of what is falling apart, and the journals the students keep asking for.
purse.line: The boxes come in October and the students carry them up. The lector says nothing, which from him is thanks.

purse.label: The fabric of the house
purse.blurb: The roof, the boiler, the choir stalls with the loose backs, the room nobody uses because of the damp.
purse.line: The scaffolding is up for a season. The old men complain about the noise and then about the cold when it comes down, and the house is warmer for it for years.

purse.label: The guest wing
purse.blurb: Beds made, a chaplain's welcome, retreatants and the priests of the diocese who need a week away from the phone.
purse.line: The guests come, and the house learns again what it is like to be looked at. A pastor of the diocese stays a week and preaches about it afterwards.

purse.label: The door
purse.blurb: What the house gives at the door and through the parish's own society: food, the bus fare, the electric bill nobody else will pay.
purse.line: The line at the door gets longer, which is the point and also the problem. The porter asks for a second man on Tuesdays.

purse.label: The house's holiday
purse.blurb: A week at the lake, the whole house, the cook included. The Rule says recreation; the province says the money.
purse.line: The old men swim. Somebody's brother lends the boats. The house comes back tanned and easier with itself for a season.

purse.label: A man sent to study
purse.blurb: A licence course for the brightest of the young men, at the province's studium or abroad. Two years of his absence, and the house pays for the plane.
purse.line: He goes in September. The house is a man short at the Hours and the provincial writes to say it was the right thing, which he does not often write.

purse.label: A vocations weekend
purse.blurb: Open the house for a weekend: the Office, the table, the men who might come, and the ones who came last year to say why.
purse.line: Eleven young men and one who was not young. Two write afterwards. The house talked about them at recreation for a week, which is what the weekend is for.

builds.label: Restore the chapel
builds.blurb: The choir stalls, the floor, the roof over the sanctuary, and light where there was none. The house prays there five times a day and has stopped seeing it.
builds.line: The scaffolding comes down in Lent and the house sings Vespers in a room it can see again.

builds.label: A library wing
builds.blurb: Shelves for what is in boxes, a reading room, and a place for the lector's books when he dies, which he has been mentioning.
builds.line: The books go up in a week and the men go in and do not come out, which the prior counts as success.

builds.label: Build a guest wing
builds.blurb: Twelve rooms, a chapel of their own, and a door the retreatants can use without walking through the cloister.
builds.line: The first retreat fills it. A pastor of the diocese stays a week and preaches about it, and two of his young men come to look at the house afterwards.

builds.label: Enlarge the church
builds.blurb: The nave lengthened, the side chapels opened, room for the people who stand at the back on feasts. The bishop's office has a view; so does the diocesan architect.
builds.line: The church is consecrated again with the bishop, and full, and stays fuller than it was, and the house is known in the city for a building for the first time in a century.

builds.label: Build classrooms
builds.blurb: Four rooms and a lecture hall: the house teaches, or begins to. The lay Dominicans come on Tuesdays and the diocese's catechists on Thursdays.
builds.line: The first course is on the Creed, with forty in the room. The house has a school of sorts now, and men who wanted to teach have somewhere to.

builds.label: A new wing for the studium
builds.blurb: Twelve more cells, a second lecture hall, and the province's students no longer two to a room. The province will send men it could not house.
builds.line: The wing opens in September with every cell taken, and the master of students, who did not want it, says at chapter that he was wrong, which is a thing the house will tell for years.

builds.label: Enlarge the novitiate
builds.blurb: Eight more cells and a second chapter room, for the years the province has more novices than beds.
builds.line: The novice master walks the new corridor the day it opens and says it will be full in two years, and it is.

builds.label: Found a school
builds.blurb: A high school of the order's own, on the house's land or the parish's: a principal from the house, lay teachers, and four hundred boys in ten years. The largest thing a house can do, and the one the province remembers a prior for.
builds.line: The school opens with ninety boys in a building that smells of paint, a principal who has not slept, and a house that is now a school's house and will be for a hundred years.
